name: bpd
description: registers bpd as a debug adapter, so a launch configuration can name it

untrustedWorkspaces.description: a launch configuration names an interpreter and a program, and starting a session runs both

virtualWorkspaces.description: bpd spawns a local interpreter and binds breakpoints against files on disk

bpd.executable.markdownDescription: the `bpd` command to start `bpd dap` with. a bare name is looked up on `PATH`; anything else must be an absolute path. a relative path is refused rather than resolved against a directory nobody chose

args.description: arguments for the program, exactly as it receives them

python.description: the interpreter to run under, resolved on PATH like any other command

stopOnEntry.description: stay stopped before the program's first statement. bpd holds every program there — it is how a breakpoint binds against a real interpreter — so this decides whether the client is told about it, not whether it happens

justMyCode.description: stop and step only in the program's own code: an exception a library raises and catches is not a stop, one it raises into the program stops where it arrives there, and a step in goes through a library's code to the next function of the program's it calls. a library is a frozen module, `<string>`, or a file under the standard library or a site-packages directory of the interpreter running the program

inheritStdin.description: give the program the stdin `bpd dap --listen` was started with rather than an empty one. refused over stdio, where that stdin is the protocol. for a client that started the adapter itself with a stdin meant for the program, as `by run --launcher` does with the run's console

launcher.description: the program is a launcher: a script that makes the program being debugged `__main__` and runs it, the way `by run`'s `_by_runner.py` does. its own frames are how the program was started, so no stack shows them, no step lands in them, and an exception the program does not catch stops in the program's outermost frame below them

stopTheWorld.description: hold every thread that can be held for the duration of each stop. off by default: a stop holds one thread and the rest of the program keeps running. a thread parked in a C call cannot be held and is named rather than counted as held

exceptionClasses.description: a rule per exception class, armed before the program runs a line. each decides for its class and every subclass, the nearest class's rule deciding, in place of the raised and uncaught filters. beside the exception options rather than through them: where both name a class, this one decides

name.description: the class as module.QualName, or a builtin's bare name: ValueError, json.decoder.JSONDecodeError

uncaught.description: stop where one leaves the program

libraries.description: stop where a library's code raises one, rather than where it first arrives in the program's own code

debugChildren.description: debug a child the program forks. off by default: a debugged fork stops at the line that forked, and a second debug session is started for it through the startDebugging reverse request. it needs bpd to be reachable by a second connection, which means `bpd dap --listen`. a child that was exec'd rather than forked is a fresh interpreter and is reported rather than debugged

watchRecompositions.description: turn on basedpython-ui's recomposition stream before the program runs a line, so the first frame is seen. off by default: with it on, every composable that runs is reported on the debug console with why it ran

console.description: where the program runs, and therefore what its standard streams are. the debug console is pipes bpd forwards as output events, with /dev/null for stdin — so isatty() is False and input() raises EOFError. either terminal is the runInTerminal reverse request: vs code starts the program in a terminal it owns, so the program has a real one and reads real input, and its output goes to that terminal rather than to the debug console

threadSettleMs.description: how far apart the two samples a thread census compares are taken

variables.description: how much of a value to read, and what the debugger may run to read it. a value that hits one of these bounds says which one, so this is where it gets raised

depth.description: how many levels of container or object to open. zero reports a value's type and size and opens nothing

children.description: how many children of one container to read

text.description: how many characters of one string, or bytes of one bytes, to read

budget.description: the byte budget for the whole answer. when it runs out the answer says so at the point it ran out

attributes.description: read an object's instance dictionary. it is storage rather than behaviour for an ordinary object, and never reaches __getattr__ or a property — turn it off for a program full of proxies, whose __dict__ is their own code

repr.description: call __repr__ on a value with no structural representation. off by default because __repr__ is arbitrary user code that bpd cannot interrupt once it has started

configurationSnippets.description: run the open file under bpd

configurationSnippets.label: bpd: debug a program, stopped at entry
configurationSnippets.description: run a program under bpd and stay stopped before its first statement
